source_text: וְ/נָטִ֤יתִי אֶת יָדִ/י֙ עֲלֵי/הֶ֔ם וְ/נָתַתִּ֨י אֶת הָ/אָ֜רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֤ה וּ/מְשַׁמָּה֙ מִ/מִּדְבַּ֣ר דִּבְלָ֔תָ/ה בְּ/כֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֽוֹתֵי/הֶ֑ם וְ/יָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה־־־׃פ
english_snapshot: So I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolation and a waste[a], from the wilderness toward Diblath, throughout all their settlements[b]. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'from the wilderness toward Diblath.' The place name is uncertain; some understand 'from the wilderness to Diblath,' and some textual proposals relate it to Riblah.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ/י֮ הֲ/רָאִ֣יתָ בֶן אָדָם֒ הֲ/נָקֵל֙ לְ/בֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה מֵ/עֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת הַ/תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשׂוּ פֹ֑ה כִּֽי מָלְא֨וּ אֶת הָ/אָ֜רֶץ חָמָ֗ס וַ/יָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ לְ/הַכְעִיסֵ֔/נִי וְ/הִנָּ֛/ם שֹׁלְחִ֥ים אֶת הַ/זְּמוֹרָ֖ה אֶל אַפָּֽ/ם־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then he said to me[a], “Have you seen, son of man? Is it too trivial a thing for the house of Judah to do the abominations that they have done here, that they should also fill the land with violence and turn again to provoke me? And behold[b], they are putting the branch to their nose.”

signals.text: Or, following some ancient witnesses, “they are putting the branch to my nose.” The Hebrew text reads “their nose.”

source_text: וְ/נָתַתִּ֤י לָ/הֶם֙ לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֔ד וְ/ר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּ/קִרְבְּ/כֶ֑ם וַ/הֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י לֵ֤ב הָ/אֶ֨בֶן֙ מִ/בְּשָׂרָ֔/ם וְ/נָתַתִּ֥י לָ/הֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר׃
english_snapshot: And I will give them one heart[a], and I will put a new spirit within them[b]. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh.

signals.text: Hebrew textual form here can be read 'within you'; the sense in context is commonly taken as 'within them,' matching the surrounding pronouns and the close parallel in Ezekiel 36:26.

source_text: לְמַ֨עַן טְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֨בַח֙ הוּחַ֔דָּה לְמַעַן הֱיֵה לָ֥/הּ בָּ֖רָק מֹרָ֑טָּה א֣וֹ נָשִׂ֔ישׂ שֵׁ֥בֶט בְּנִ֖/י מֹאֶ֥סֶת כָּל עֵֽץ־־־׃
english_snapshot: So that it may slaughter a slaughter[a], it is sharpened; so that it may have a flash, it is polished[b]. Or shall we rejoice? The scepter of my son despises every tree.

signals.text: Hebrew is difficult in the final clause. 'My son' follows the Masoretic Text; some interpreters understand it more broadly of Judah or my people, and 'every tree' may mean every wooden staff or weapon.

source_text: וַ/יָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֔י/הָ כְּ/ב֖וֹא אֶל אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן בָּ֗אוּ אֶֽל אָֽהֳלָה֙ וְ/אֶל אָ֣הֳלִיבָ֔ה אִשֹּׁ֖ת הַ/זִּמָּֽה־־־׃
english_snapshot: They went in to her as men go in to a prostitute[a]; so they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah[b], women of depravity.

signals.text: Or, more formally, 'He came to her as one goes in to a prostitute; so they came to Oholah and to Oholibah.' The Hebrew opens with a singular verb before shifting to plural.

source_text: לָ/כֵן֩ הִנְ/נִ֨י פֹתֵ֜חַ אֶת כֶּ֤תֶף מוֹאָב֙ מֵ/הֶ֣/עָרִ֔ים מֵֽ/עָרָ֖י/ו מִ/קָּצֵ֑/הוּ צְבִ֗י אֶ֚רֶץ בֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁימֹ֔ת בַּ֥עַל מְע֖וֹן ו/קריתמ/ה־׃
english_snapshot: Therefore behold[a], I am opening the flank of Moab from its cities, from its frontier cities, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon[c][b], and Kiriathaim.

signals.text: Hebrew text has a spelling form for the final place name corresponding to Kiriathaim, a known Moabite city.

source_text: וְדָ֤ן וְ/יָוָן֙ מְ/אוּזָּ֔ל בְּ/עִזְבוֹנַ֖יִ/ךְ נָתָ֑נּוּ בַּרְזֶ֤ל עָשׁוֹת֙ קִדָּ֣ה וְ/קָנֶ֔ה בְּ/מַעֲרָבֵ֖/ךְ הָיָֽה׃
english_snapshot: Dan and Javan from Uzal traded with you[a]; they exchanged wrought iron, cassia[c][b], and cane for your wares.

signals.text: Hebrew 'Dan'; some read 'Vedan' or otherwise emend the name because the text is difficult.

source_text: וְ/נָשְׂא֨וּ אֵלַ֤יִ/ךְ בְּ/נִי/הֶם֙ קִינָ֔ה וְ/קוֹנְנ֖וּ עָלָ֑יִ/ךְ מִ֣י כְ/צ֔וֹר כְּ/דֻמָ֖ה בְּ/ת֥וֹךְ הַ/יָּֽם׃
english_snapshot: They will raise a lamentation over you in their wailing[a], and they will lament over you: ‘Who is like Tyre[b], silenced in the midst of the sea?’

signals.text: The phrase rendered 'in their wailing' is textually and lexically difficult; some understand it differently, including readings related to 'their sons.' The mourning context favors the sense of lamenting cry.

source_text: אַ֨תְּ כְּר֔וּב מִמְשַׁ֖ח הַ/סּוֹכֵ֑ךְ וּ/נְתַתִּ֗י/ךָ בְּ/הַ֨ר קֹ֤דֶשׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ הָיִ֔יתָ בְּ/ת֥וֹךְ אַבְנֵי אֵ֖שׁ הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ־־׃
english_snapshot: You were an anointed guardian cherub[a], and I placed you on the holy mountain of God[b]; you walked in the midst of stones of fire.

signals.text: The Hebrew text begins with a feminine-form pronoun ('you'), while the surrounding verbs and suffixes are masculine; the sense is still singular 'you.'

source_text: כִּֽי נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת חתית/ו בְּ/אֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֑ים וְ/הֻשְׁכַּב֩ בְּ/ת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֜ים אֶת חַלְלֵי חֶ֗רֶב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְ/כָל הֲמוֹנֹ֔/ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥/י יְהוִֽה־־־־־׃פ
english_snapshot: For I put his terror in the land of the living[a], and he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.

signals.text: Or, following some ancient witnesses: “my terror in the land of the living.” The Hebrew text here reads “his terror.”

source_text: וְ/לֹא אַשְׁמִ֨יעַ אֵלַ֤יִ/ךְ עוֹד֙ כְּלִמַּ֣ת הַ/גּוֹיִ֔ם וְ/חֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖ים לֹ֣א תִשְׂאִי ע֑וֹד ו/גוי/ך לֹא תַכְשִׁ֣לִי ע֔וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥/י יְהוִֽה־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: And I will no longer let you hear the disgrace of the nations[a], and you will no longer bear the reproach of the peoples, and you will no longer cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.

signals.text: Or 'make your nation fall' or, following another interpretive tradition, 'bereave your nation.' The Hebrew consonantal text here is difficult; the Masoretic vocalization supports 'cause your nation to stumble.'

source_text: וְ/עַ֗ל פְּנֵי֙ הַ/שַּׁ֣עַר ה/יאתון עַל לִ/פְנֵ֕י אֻלָ֥ם הַ/שַּׁ֖עַר הַ/פְּנִימִ֑י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים אַמָּֽה־׃
english_snapshot: And from the front of the outer gateway to the front of the vestibule of the inner gate was fifty cubits[a][b][c].

signals.text: Hebrew text is difficult at 'the outer gateway'; the underlying term is unusual here. Many interpreters understand it to mean the outer gate/gateway from the context of the surrounding measurements.

source_text: וְ/לִ/פְנֵ֨י הַ/לְּשָׁכ֜וֹת מַהֲלַךְ֩ עֶ֨שֶׂר אַמּ֥וֹת רֹ֨חַב֙ אֶל הַ/פְּנִימִ֔ית דֶּ֖רֶךְ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּ/פִתְחֵי/הֶ֖ם לַ/צָּפֽוֹן־׃
english_snapshot: Before the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide toward the inner court[a], and a passage one cubit wide[b]; and their entrances faced north.

signals.text: The Hebrew text is difficult in this clause. Some understand it as 'a way of one cubit' or, following a different vocalization/tradition, 'one hundred cubits.'

source_text: מָדַ֛ד ר֥וּחַ הַ/קָּדִ֖ים בִּ/קְנֵ֣ה הַ/מִּדָּ֑ה חֲמֵשׁ אמות קָנִ֛ים בִּ/קְנֵ֥ה הַ/מִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב־׃
english_snapshot: He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed[a], all around.

signals.text: Hebrew literally reads 'five cubits, reeds.' In context, this is commonly understood as 'five hundred reeds,' in harmony with the surrounding measurements (vv. 16–19). Some manuscripts and ancient versions reflect this more explicitly.

source_text: מָדַ֖ד ר֣וּחַ הַ/צָּפ֑וֹן חֲמֵשׁ מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֛ים בִּ/קְנֵ֥ה הַ/מִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב־׃
english_snapshot: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds[a], by the measuring reed all around.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'five hundred reeds.' Some manuscripts and ancient versions have a reading reflected in some translations as 'five hundred cubits.' The main text follows the Masoretic Hebrew here.

source_text: אֵ֛ת ר֥וּחַ הַ/דָּר֖וֹם מָדָ֑ד חֲמֵשׁ מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֖ים בִּ/קְנֵ֥ה הַ/מִּדָּֽה־׃
english_snapshot: He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts and ancient versions read 'cubits' instead of 'reeds' in this measurement context; the Masoretic Text reads 'reeds.'

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗/י הַ/מַּ֤יִם הָ/אֵ֨לֶּה֙ יוֹצְאִ֗ים אֶל הַ/גְּלִילָה֙ הַ/קַּדְמוֹנָ֔ה וְ/יָרְד֖וּ עַל הָֽ/עֲרָבָ֑ה וּ/בָ֣אוּ הַ/יָּ֔מָּ/ה אֶל הַ/יָּ֥מָּ/ה הַ/מּֽוּצָאִ֖ים ו/נרפאו הַ/מָּֽיִם־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then he said to me[a], “These waters flow out toward the eastern district and go down into the Arabah; then they enter the sea. and when they are brought out into the sea[c][b], the waters are healed.”

signals.text: Or 'the Dead Sea.' The Hebrew expression is difficult and is commonly understood as referring to the salt sea east of Judah.

source_text: וּ/פְאַ֣ת קָדִ֡ים מִ/בֵּ֣ין חַוְרָ֣ן וּ/מִ/בֵּין דַּמֶּשֶׂק֩ וּ/מִ/בֵּ֨ין הַ/גִּלְעָ֜ד וּ/מִ/בֵּ֨ין אֶ֤רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִ/גְּב֛וּל עַל הַ/יָּ֥ם הַ/קַּדְמוֹנִ֖י תָּמֹ֑דּוּ וְ/אֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת קָדִֽימָ/ה־־׃
english_snapshot: And the eastern side shall be from between Hauran and Damascus[a], and between Gilead and the land of Israel, the Jordan, from the border to the eastern sea; you shall measure the eastern side.

signals.text: Or, more specifically, 'the Dead Sea'; Hebrew: 'the eastern sea.'
